parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing border, document or facility restrictions are documented, and private same-sex conduct was never criminalised — but the public-decency provision with an aggravated same-sex clause and unequal age of consent is an unenforced-yet-available police lever. The dominant exposure is societal: a documented late-2024 wave (45 assaults in two months, influencer calls to violence), trans-feminine people singled out for the harshest violence, three community deaths in 2023, historic security-force raids and beatings of transvestis, and police who blame victims and deter reporting. That is tier-3 hostility with thin recourse, plus latent state threat-framing (president's promised bill, outcome unknown). This sits above the 0.35 anchors (no universal-exposure state machinery) but below 0.55 anchors (their harms are administrative; here violence is patterned and underprotected). Foreigner/wealth status may soften street hostility but is not a documented protection. No minor-specific regime documented; the 18-vs-15 consent asymmetry is a secondary lever.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented — no reports of marker-mismatch questioning, secondary screening or denial at borders.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; no local marker process touches it.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Historic security-force raids, forced undressing and extortion targeting transvestis (2010-2012); no current prisoner-placement data either way.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Decency statute could ground arrest if outed publicly.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Healthcare discrimination documented (doctor refused service); no facility bans aimed at visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Emergency care could expose trans status with no anti-discrimination recourse.

care_services.exposure: Documented refusal of care on orientation grounds; medication/HRT access for visitors not addressed.
care_services.protection: Protest secured care in one dated case — not a functioning regime.
care_services.interaction: Refusal intersects with policing: outing during treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 360 aggravates same-sex indecency; unequal age of consent (18 vs 15); president's promised anti-'expansion' bill unresolved; historic state-force violence against trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Human Rights Council's 2024 statement urging tolerance — rhetorical, limited.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute is a latent lever amid social hostility; enforcement currently not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Doubled penalty if same-sex act occurs with or before a minor; conversion therapy (prayer camp) documented, including a trans man's suicide attempt.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling parent could face heightened scrutiny if outed with a minor; age-of-consent asymmetry is a lever.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 45 assaults in two months (2024), influencer-incited violence, three deaths in 2023, market attack, trans-feminine people at highest risk; hypervigilance reported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police handling described as improving but slow, victim-blaming; Council statement only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Underreporting and impunity leave visitors without realistic recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No GI anti-discrimination protection; no sourced hate-crime statute; custody placement, current tolerance toward trans people, and fate of 2024 bill all unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional/treaty rights invoked by the Council — untested.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documented border friction is not evidence of safety; unknowns resolve toward risk given hostile social climate.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A rests on a universal-exposure state machine (visitor register, routine border exclusion). This jurisdiction lacks any documented traveller-facing state machinery; its harms are societal violence plus a latent statute, so it rates above it.

0.55-B's worst documented outcome is administrative (denied entry, missed connections) with appeals existing. Here the worst documented outcomes are beatings, deaths and victim-blaming police with no effective remedy — materially worse, so below 0.55.

0.15-C features organised morality-unit sweeps, coerced detention and failing courts. This jurisdiction's state targeting is dated (2010-2012), current violence is societal with improving (if weak) police handling, and no execution pathway is documented — clearly above 0.15.

0.45-A couples universal biometric exposure with a deceptive-presentation statute. This jurisdiction lacks universal-exposure measures but has far heavier documented street violence against trans people, placing it near but slightly below 0.45's band midpoint.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines (i) no entry/document barriers for visitors, (ii) a latent decency statute with a same-sex aggravator usable as a police lever, (iii) a documented, recent, patterned wave of societal anti-trans violence in which trans-feminine people are primary targets, (iv) state institutions that historically attacked trans people and now respond slowly and with victim-blaming, and (v) no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse documented. Visitor-specific exposures (documents, custody, facilities) are largely undocumented, which keeps the score out of the High-Risk band's depths; but under the rubric the absence of evidence is not safety, and thin-data extrapolation from a criminalising-adjacent statute, a hostile state trajectory, and documented impunity resolves toward risk. Foreigner and wealth status may reduce street hostility but are not protections. Net: Elevated Risk, low end of the band.
